Stated Claim / Post Context:
‘Put His 5-Year-Old In Danger’: Mullin Clashes With Margaret Brennan Over ICE Shooting Of Criminal Illegal

‘because of the selfish behavior’

Actual Article Body:
Screenshot/Rumble/CBS News

Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told CBS News’ Margaret Brennan that body camera footage would not tell the whole story of a Thursday shooting involving immigration agents and a criminal illegal immigrant — adding that the foreign national put his own son at risk.

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent opened fire at Dominican national Oscar Belgal, 28, on Thursday, after the man alleged to have a lengthy and violent rap sheet accelerated his SUV toward multiple officers, authorities say. Mullin appeared on “Face the Nation” on Sunday to discuss the fallout over the New York City incident — which began to receive national attention especially after it was revealed Belgal’s 5-year-old son was in the backseat of the SUV.

“We had our badges out, once again, giving lawful demands. He decided that he was going to accelerate and try to evade again,” Mullin recounted Thursday’s events to Brennan. “We had taken every precaution to try to keep that from happening, and unfortunately, this took place. We would have loved for him to exit the vehicle, like we asked him to. He decided not to. Unfortunately, because of the selfish behavior, he put his 5-year-old in danger.” (RELATED: Markwayne Mullin Reminds Jake Tapper What the ‘T’ in ‘TPS’ Means)

WATCH:

Belgal was treated for his injuries from the shooting and is currently in a detention center, according to NewsNation.

Socialist Democratic New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani publicly denounced the shooting and presence of ICE in New York. Mamdani spoke to Mullin and President Donald Trump for two hours Thursday night, during which the socialist mayor unsuccessfully lobbied for Belgal’s release, Time reported.

Body camera footage of the incident from the point of view of the ICE agent who shot Belgal had not yet been released as of Sunday afternoon. However, footage from body cameras worn by New York Police Department (NYPD) officers who arrived on the scene was released shortly after the incident.

Belgal entered the country illegally and has alleged ties to a violent Dominican-American gang, according to the DHS.

“What you’re not seeing is the actual audio footage or a different angle, where you have multiple officers who are approaching this individual named Oscar, with a long, very long extensive rap sheet,” Mullin told Brennan after she asked him when the ICE agent’s body camera footage will be released.

He confirmed that federal authorities will release the footage once an investigation is completed.

“He’s [Belgal has] only been in the country for three years, and he has a rap sheet of four charges of felony robbery, two charges of felony assault, felony larceny … two felony charges of dangerous drugs and strong gang affiliation that has direct or indirect knowledge of a CBP [Customs and Border Protection] officer that was shot last year. And this guy evaded officers last month when we tried to get to him,” the secretary added. “We knew he was armed. We knew he was dangerous. Or there was a possibility of him being armed.”

This criminal illegal alien is the definition of worst of the worst. His criminal history includes a prior criminal conviction for fourth-degree grand larceny, prior arrests for first-degree robbery: forcible theft armed with a deadly weapon, criminal sale of a controlled substance, possession of stolen property, and assault. He has associations with the violent Trinitarios gang. New York sanctuary politicians have created an environment for criminal activity to thrive, not for American citizens to be safe.

In a Friday post to X, the DHS called Belgal “the definition of worst of the worst”

Mullin told Brennan that immigration agents did not know they would find Belgal’s young child in his vehicle, and that his father bore responsibility for putting him in the line of fire.

“We knew his pattern of life, but we didn’t know the 5-year-old was in the vehicle,” he said on CBS News. “Who did know the 5-year-old was in the vehicle was Oscar. Now as a father of six kids, no way would I ever put my kids in danger.”

Stated Claim / Post Context:
21-year-old NYC native goes to the hospital for a simple broken ankle — and dies for shocking reason: lawsuit

Dale Alice Martin's hearbroken family said in court documents that Waterbury Hospital in Connecticut disastrously botched the college student's care for an ankle fracture in April 2025.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A 21-year-old Manhattan native went to a hospital to be treated for a simple broken ankle — only to end up dead because she was given too many painkillers, according to a shocking lawsuit.

The heartbroken family of tragic Dale Alice Martin said in court documents that Waterbury Hospital in Connecticut disastrously botched the college student’s care April 10, 2025, when she arrived there to be treated for the ankle she fractured while doing farm work — and was given a lethal cocktail of drugs that left her brain-dead, the Hartford Courant reported.

“We didn’t know till after Dale’s death that she was admitted to a bankrupt hospital that was under investigation, where nurses allegedly were buying food for patients, where the level of funding was so constrained that the hospital may not have been able to function properly,” said the dead woman’s father, Westchester County resident Lindsay Martin, to the outlet.

“Dale did not have a choice of where to go,” he said of his daughter, a Bethlehem, Connecticut, resident who attended middle and high school in Pelham in Westechester and was an English and history student at Trinity University in San Antonio, Texas, according to the Pelham Examiner.

“She was brought to the nearest hospital,” the dad noted.

An autopsy determined that Dale died from cardiac arrest after being given multiple painkillers, according to the suit filed by family lawyer Christopher Mattei.

“Within 14 hours of admission, providers at the hospital had administered so much pain medication that Dale stopped breathing and later died,” the lawsuit said. “No one checked on Dale during this time.

“The same medications that were interfering with Dale’s breathing were also sedating her. Dale could not even call for help as she suffocated. At 7 a.m. on April 10, a Waterbury Hospital nurse finally checked on Dale. It was far too late. Her heart had stopped beating.”

Lindsay Martin said he remembers the dreadful phone call from the hospital when she died.

“I hung up the phone, and I was in shock,” the dad said.

The family had been unaware of the issues with the hospital, which was long owned by California-based Prospect Medical Holdings, a company that filed for bankruptcy in January 2025.

Earlier this year, Hartford HealthCare bought the struggling facility and two others.

“What we expect to find is that this was a hospital that was largely operating on fumes as a result of Prospect dismantling infrastructure within the hospital, reducing staff, training, and finding every way possible to extract value out of the hospital in a way that jeopardized care,” Mattei said.

A rep for the hospital declined to comment because Dale’s death predated its ownership.

The former CEOs of Prospect, David Topper and Von Crockett, did not respond to calls and emails from WNBC-TV News seeking comment on the lawsuit.
